escapeSemantics: result.json escapedBugs = held-out failures at declared-done and heldoutPassed = passes (run-pair.sh extract_metrics; a non-compiling final state counts as ALL tests failing), and taskSuccess is escapedBugs == 0. PP-W-rows does NOT read escapedBugs as its leg-A escape: ESCAPE = at least one of tests.effectObservingTests failed on a workspace that BUILT. A run whose declared-done state does not build — the shape arm B's shortcut takes, and any budget exhaustion — is NOT an escape; it is published as its own category (non-building declared-done), because scoring it as up to heldoutTestCount escapes would invert leg A's sign against the arm whose compiler refuses the laundering.

shapeRealizedIndicator.name: field- or property-stored stage
shapeRealizedIndicator.question: the final source keeps the step as class state — a function-typed §FLD or §PROP in RetryBehavior — and Twice passes it to RunTwice
shapeRealizedIndicator.reportedBy: ppw-analyze.py, per cell, beside the escape rate
shapeRealizedIndicator.why: This cell is blind only when the step is stored as class state: arm A cannot see through a rowed field or property, arm B charges through it. The natural spellings are pushed away — a printing §LAM inside a §CTOR is error Calor0422 on BOTH arms, and a bare module-level method group is Calor1002 (#1118) — so an agent reaching for the natural spelling can land on the W-001s lambda shape instead, which arm A WARNS about, silently degrading this cell to warning-vs-error at run time. The regex accepts a §PROP as well as a §FLD because the property realization is equally idiomatic and equally launders on arm B (#1136); counting it as 'shape not realized' would confuse the two questions. Recorded, never scored.
